exposure: emergency or planned caesarean delivery in labour or prelabour
cohort: Women who gave birth in Denmark between 2004 and 2010 (n=450,856)
finding: Intended cesarean delivery was significantly associated with a higher risk of postpartum urinary tract infection compared with intended vaginal delivery, even after adjusting for potential confounders.
mod_finding: All types of operative delivery had an equally increased risk of postpartum urinary tract infection compared with spontaneous vaginal delivery.
